Capture-name contract (parser_elements.rs 285-296): 'function' with 'func_name' or 'method_name'; 'class' with 'class_name' or 'type_name'; 'call'; 'import_path'; 'type_ref'; DEFUSE prefixes 'write.', 'read.', 'writeread.' (parser_elements.rs 878-883).
Java pattern: ELEMENT_QUERY pairs method_declaration with @function and captures name as @method_name; class-like kinds share @class (java.rs 4-14).

Java DEFUSE_QUERY pattern: declaration write (local_variable_declaration), assignment write (assignment_expression left), writeread for update_expression, catch-all (identifier) @read.usage (java.rs 32-37).

approaches.name: A. Java/Swift-shaped handler on LANGUAGE_PHP (recommended)
approaches.description: Add crates/aptu-coder-core/src/languages/php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY (function_definition, method_declaration, class/interface/trait/enum_declaration), CALL_QUERY (function, member, scoped calls), REFERENCE_QUERY (named_type), IMPORT_QUERY (namespace_use_declaration via the parser's full-text fallback), DEFUSE_QUERY (assignment, static/param write, augmented/update, variable_name reads) and extract_inheritance that walks the unfielded base_clause and class_interface_clause children. Grammar entry point is tree_sitter_php::LANGUAGE_PHP (not LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY, which rejects HTML text). Wire php in languages/mod.rs (pub mod, get_language_info arm, get_ts_language arm, table test), lang.rs (EXTENSION_MAP entry, supported_languages entry, extension test), Cargo.toml workspace and core crate, Cargo.lock, README, and an integration test file.
pros: Matches the issue scope and its five-constant contract exactly
Same registry shape as java/swift/css, so reviewers know it
LANGUAGE_PHP handles mixed HTML through the text and text_interpolation extras, so the template acceptance criterion is achievable without special-casing
Inheritance handler covers class, interface (extends list), and enum (implements) with one walk
cons: DEFUSE captures bare name nodes under variable_name, so symbol matching requires the caller to pass 'x' without the '$' sigil; needs documenting
Import capture stores the whole statement text via the fallback arm (same as Java/Swift), not structured items
Trait use, property and constant extraction are out of scope and will be absent
tree-sitter-php 0.25.2 GitHub release is dated 2026-11-19; the 7-day package-age gate for new Cargo.lock entries must be checked against the crates.io publish date (fallback 0.25.1, 2026-10-06)
Queries are derived from node-types.json and grammar.js, not yet compiled; the unit test is the first proof

approaches.name: B. Minimal-first: five-constant shell with DEFUSE and REFERENCE disabled
approaches.description: Same php.rs file and wiring as A, but set reference_query: None and defuse_query: None in the registry and ship only ELEMENT, CALL, IMPORT and extract_inheritance; add DEFUSE in a follow-up issue.
pros: Smallest parser surface and fewest query-compile risks
Avoids the '$'-stripped symbol-matching question until a consumer needs it
Fastest path to a green cargo deny, clippy and test run
cons: Conflicts with the issue, which lists DEFUSE_QUERY among the five required constants
Leaves PHP without def-use sites, so analysis features that depend on defuse return nothing for .php
Implies a second PR, and the binary size delta would be measured twice

approaches.name: C. Start from upstream queries/tags.scm and rewrite to aptu capture names
approaches.description: Use the grammar's own queries/tags.scm (MIT) as the source for ELEMENT and CALL patterns, including its reference.implementation pattern for class_interface_clause and object_creation_expression reference.class, then rename captures from @name/@definition.class/@reference.call to the aptu contract (function, func_name, method_name, class, class_name, call). Same wiring as A.
pros: Patterns come from the grammar maintainers and track grammar changes
Adds 'new Foo' object creation as a reference site, which A does not capture
Gives a cross-check on A's element patterns
cons: tags.scm uses a different capture vocabulary, so every capture must be renamed and re-verified against parser_elements.rs
Brings reference and implementation semantics beyond the issue scope
DEFUSE still has to be hand-written; tags.scm has no equivalent

recommendation: Approach A. It is the only option that satisfies the issue's five-constant contract and its mixed-HTML acceptance criterion while staying within the Java/Swift template. Its main risks are the '$'-stripped DEFUSE symbol matching and the cargo-deny package-age gate for tree-sitter-php 0.25.2; if the age gate fails, pin 0.25.1 (2026-10-06). Approach B is the fallback only if DEFUSE noise breaks tests, and it needs an explicit issue amendment. Before implementing, compile all five queries in a unit test (the issue's own step 3) because they were not compiled in this read-only run.

inheritance_walk_citation:
Grammar source: php/grammar.js and common/define-grammar.js at tag v0.25.2 (commit c1e13490bd656b8869cd47e6f74997ed46750a08; php/src/node-types.json is byte-identical to master).
1. class_declaration (rule: prec.right(seq(optional attributes, repeat _modifier, keyword('class'), field('name', name), optional(base_clause), optional(class_interface_clause), field('body', declaration_list)))). node-types fields: attributes, body, name. There is NO 'superclass' or 'interfaces' field, so child_by_field_name("superclass") and ("interfaces") (the Java approach) return None.
2. The class name is child_by_field_name("name") (node kind 'name').
3. Extends: base_clause is an UNFIELDED named child of class_declaration (node-types children list includes base_clause). Rule: base_clause: seq(keyword('extends'), commaSep1($._name)). Its named children are name | qualified_name | relative_name (_name is a hidden choice). The keyword token 'extends' is anonymous and skipped by named_child iteration. Walk: for each named child c of the class node with c.kind()=="base_clause", for each named child n of c with kind in {name, qualified_name, relative_name}, emit format!("extends {text(n)}").
4. Implements: class_interface_clause is an UNFIELDED named child of class_declaration. Rule: class_interface_clause: seq(keyword('implements'), commaSep1($._name)). Walk: for each named child c with kind()=="class_interface_clause", for each named child n with kind in {name, qualified_name, relative_name}, emit format!("implements {text(n)}").
5. Ordering: base_clause precedes class_interface_clause in the rule, so output order is extends-first, then implements in source order, matching the issue's expected ["extends Bar", "implements A", "implements B"].
6. No clauses: neither child exists, so the walk returns an empty Vec (issue edge case).
7. Caveat: parser_elements.rs (line 398-400) calls extract_inheritance for every @class match, including interface_declaration (rule: optional(base_clause) with extends lists, multiple allowed), enum_declaration (optional(seq(':', primitive_type)) then optional(class_interface_clause), no extends) and trait_declaration (no clauses). The same two-kind walk covers all of them; the handler must not assume kind == class_declaration (Swift's handler returns early on kind mismatch at swift.rs line 50; the PHP handler should not return early for interface/enum).
